scope: sanitized public read-only Starbucks web evidence plus one private, non-materialized disclosure signal

findings.title: Public careers configuration contains a credential-like secret signal
findings.surface: public careers integration configuration; exact routes withheld
findings.claim: A populated OAuth client-secret field was observed on more than one public Starbucks careers page, but the public repository intentionally withholds the affected routes and underlying material pending coordinated disclosure.

causal_memory.surface_scope: public Starbucks careers pages using the shared third-party integration
causal_memory.state_scope: client-readable integration configuration and credential secrecy
causal_memory.time_scope: passive observation on 2026-07-19; exact evidence withheld pending disclosure

user_control.user_effect: The credential owner may have lost secrecy and must rotate and review use, while downstream candidate or API impact remains unproven.

findings.minimal_fix: Privately validate the affected client identifier, rotate the secret, remove it from all client-rendered configuration, and review token issuance and API logs.
findings.regression_test: Fail a public-build fixture whenever serialized client configuration contains a populated clientSecret, private key, bearer token, or client-credentials secret.

findings.title: Critical public routes terminate at a JavaScript-required message
findings.surface: menu, store locator, sign-in, rewards, and gift routes
findings.claim: Five critical public routes expose only a JavaScript-required terminal response to the non-JavaScript text client, without route-specific content or recovery guidance.

causal_memory.state_scope: non-JavaScript response, route purpose, fallback content, and recovery guidance

user_control.user_effect: When scripts are unavailable, a visitor cannot inspect the menu, find a store, sign in, inspect rewards, or reach gift-card content from these route responses.

findings.minimal_fix: Return route-specific server-rendered purpose, critical read-only content where practical, and clear retry or support guidance instead of one terminal message.
findings.regression_test: For each critical route, run a no-JavaScript response contract test and assert meaningful route identity, recovery guidance, and a non-empty accessible main landmark.

findings.title: The public sitemap repeats canonical product URLs
findings.claim: The sitemap emits identical canonical product URLs under multiple menu category sections.

causal_memory.state_scope: category membership and canonical product URL identity

user_control.user_effect: Direct customer harm is not demonstrated; the repeated inventory may create avoidable crawl and indexing noise.

findings.minimal_fix: Deduplicate the normalized canonical URL set after category expansion and before sitemap serialization.
findings.regression_test: Generate the sitemap, normalize URLs, and assert that total URL count equals unique canonical URL count.

findings.title: Repeated navigation markup remains an accessibility candidate
findings.surface: public homepage navigation and footer structures
findings.claim: Repeated source structures may create duplicate landmarks or focus targets, but the accessibility-tree and hidden-state behavior have not been captured.

counterfactual.required_next_sample: desktop and mobile accessibility trees, computed hidden state, landmark count, and keyboard focus order

causal_memory.state_scope: DOM duplication, computed visibility, accessibility tree, landmarks, and tab order
causal_memory.time_scope: candidate raised on 2026-07-19; runtime evidence not captured

user_control.user_effect: No assistive-technology impact is assigned until hidden duplicates or repeated focus targets are reproduced.

findings.minimal_fix: Do not change markup based on source duplication alone; first capture the accessibility tree and focus order for supported desktop and mobile states.
findings.regression_test: At each responsive breakpoint, assert unique visible landmarks and verify that hidden navigation structures are neither focusable nor exposed in the accessibility tree.

findings.title: An active exploitable credential is not proven
findings.claim: The observed credential-like value has been proven active and grants unauthorized token, API, or candidate-data access.

counterfactual.reason: No credential validation, token request, API call, authorization check, or data access was performed.

causal_memory.state_scope: credential validity, token issuance, effective scopes, and downstream data access

user_control.user_effect: No downstream access or user-data impact is assigned to an untested credential.

findings.minimal_fix: Preserve the exposure signal but do not publish exploitability or data-impact claims without owner-side validation or separately authorized evidence.
findings.regression_test: Require explicit evidence fields for credential validity, token issuance, effective authorization, and affected data before any exploitability claim can become confirmed.

findings.title: JavaScript dependency alone is not a proven WCAG violation
findings.claim: Returning a JavaScript-required message by itself proves that the routes violate WCAG A or AA.

counterfactual.reason: No supported-browser, keyboard, screen-reader, accessibility-tree, or success-criterion mapping was captured.

causal_memory.state_scope: script dependency versus supported accessibility behavior and mapped WCAG success criteria

user_control.user_effect: The route behavior remains a QA and resilience concern, but no accessibility conformance verdict is assigned automatically.

findings.minimal_fix: Keep the route-degradation finding separate from accessibility conformance and run a criterion-mapped assistive-technology experiment.
findings.regression_test: Reject any generated WCAG claim that lacks a success-criterion mapping, supported environment, user task, and reproducible assistive-technology evidence.
